name: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis

ethnicAssociations: Particularly high incidence in Western Pacific (Guam, Kii Peninsula) - historical
Slightly lower incidence in African, Asian, and Hispanic populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Gold Coast Criteria (2019) / Revised El Escorial Criteria

criteria.description: Progressive motor impairment documented by history or clinical examination with evidence of upper motor neuron (UMN) and lower motor neuron (LMN) dysfunction in at least one body region, OR LMN dysfunction in at least two body regions
Absence of alternative explanation for the clinical presentation based on investigations
EMG evidence of active and chronic denervation in clinically affected and unaffected regions
Progressive spread of symptoms within a region or to other regions

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Gold Coast Criteria: Progressive motor impairment with UMN and LMN signs in one region OR LMN signs in two regions, plus exclusion of alternative diagnoses.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Body regions: bulbar, cervical, thoracic, lumbosacral. The Gold Coast criteria simplify and improve sensitivity over El Escorial criteria. Familial ALS (~10%) and C9orf72-associated ALS may have atypical presentations.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Combined upper and lower motor neuron signs in the same limb
searchTerms: both muscle weakness and spasticity in one limb
signs of nerve damage affecting movement in same arm or leg
mixed upper and lower nerve damage symptoms in one limb

pathognomonic.notes: Preferential wasting of thenar and first dorsal interosseous over hypothenar; relatively specific to ALS
searchTerms: hand muscle wasting with split appearance
loss of muscles between thumb and fingers
claw-like hand deformity with muscle loss
muscle twitches and shrinkage of tongue

common.notes: Often starts in one limb and spreads contiguously
searchTerms: gradual uneven weakness in arms or legs
progressive muscle weakness affecting one side

common.notes: Widespread fasciculations in the context of weakness

searchTerms: increased muscle tone with exaggerated reflexes
muscle tightness and strong reflex responses

occasional.notes: Involuntary laughing or crying; UMN bulbar sign
May be presenting symptom in rare cases
Up to 50% have some cognitive involvement; ~15% meet FTD criteria
searchTerms: changes in behavior and thinking skills
difficulty with planning and social behavior

rare.notes: Mild sensory complaints present in minority; prominent sensory loss argues against ALS

laboratory: CK may be mildly to moderately elevated (typically <10x normal)
GM1 antibody testing to exclude multifocal motor neuropathy
Serum protein electrophoresis to exclude paraprotein-associated motor neuron disease
imaging: MRI brain and spine to exclude structural mimics (cervical myelopathy, tumors)
Corticospinal tract hyperintensity on FLAIR MRI (supportive but insensitive)
FDG-PET may show frontal/temporal hypometabolism in ALS-FTD
genetic: C9orf72 hexanucleotide repeat expansion (most common genetic cause; ~40% of familial ALS, ~7% sporadic)
SOD1 mutations (~20% of familial ALS; tofersen FDA-approved for SOD1-ALS)
TARDBP (TDP-43), FUS, UBQLN2, VCP, and other rare genes
Genetic counseling recommended for all ALS patients
other: EMG showing active denervation (fibrillations, positive sharp waves) and chronic reinnervation (large MUPs) in multiple regions
Nerve conduction studies: normal sensory potentials; motor amplitudes may be reduced
Transcranial magnetic stimulation may show prolonged central motor conduction time
Pulmonary function tests: reduced FVC (prognostic marker)

distinguishingFeatures: MG has fatigable weakness without atrophy or fasciculations
MG has abnormal repetitive nerve stimulation
CIDP has demyelinating features on NCS
CIDP has areflexia (vs hyperreflexia in ALS)
IBM has distal finger flexor and quadriceps weakness pattern
IBM lacks upper motor neuron signs
IBM has characteristic muscle biopsy findings

redFlags: Rapidly progressive weakness with respiratory failure requires urgent evaluation
Prominent sensory loss, sphincter involvement, or eye movement abnormalities argue against ALS
Treatable ALS mimics must be excluded: cervical myelopathy, multifocal motor neuropathy, Kennedy disease
Cognitive screening important - up to 50% have frontotemporal dysfunction
SOD1 genetic testing should be offered (FDA-approved targeted therapy available)
C9orf72 testing important for genetic counseling and clinical trials
references: Shefner JM, et al. A proposal for new diagnostic criteria for ALS. Clin Neurophysiol. 2020;131(8):1975-1978.
Brown RH, Al-Chalabi A. Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis. N Engl J Med. 2017;377(2):162-172.
Feldman EL, et al. Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Lancet. 2022;400(10360):1363-1380.
Miller TM, et al. Trial of Antisense Oligonucleotide Tofersen for SOD1 ALS. N Engl J Med. 2022;387(12):1099-1110.
